chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Mansur, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father passed by me while I was performing Tawaf, and I was young and had strived in worship, so he saw me and I was perspiring profusely. He said to me: 'O Ja'far! O my son! When Allah loves a servant, He enters him into Paradise and is pleased with him for even a little [effort].'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of moderation in worship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia principle of *al-wasatiyyah* (moderation) in worship, contrasting the rigor of the ascetics with the balanced approach favored by the Imams. Imam al-Baqir’s observation of his son’s excessive sweating during Tawaf serves as a practical lesson that divine acceptance is not contingent upon physical exhaustion, but rather on consistency and sincerity. This narrative reinforces the theological view that Allah’s mercy allows for ease, preventing believers from burning out in their spiritual pursuits.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, from Mansour, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws passed by measws and Iasws was in the Tawāf, and Iasws was young and had strived regarding the worship. So heasws saw measws, and Iasws was affected by perspiration. So heasws said to measws: ‘O Ja’farasws! O myasws sonasws! Allahazwj, when Heazwj Loves a servant, Enters him into the Paradise and is Pleased from him with the little’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from Mansur from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘

Once my father passed by during my Tawaf (walking seven times around the Ka’ba). I was young and very seriously striving to worship. He saw me sweating and said to me, “O Ja’far, my son, if Allah loves any (of His) servants, He admits him in paradise and becomes happy with him even with a very little good deed.’”
